presentation.title: Clinic reopening
presentation.context: Is the September reopening now credible enough to plan around?

whatChanged.text: The final oxygen-system inspection passed, clearing the published facility-safety blocker for the September 3 reopening.

whyItMatters.text: Staffing and patient transfers can move from contingency planning to a dated reopening sequence.

watchNext.text: Watch for the staffing roster, the remaining published checkpoint before doors can open on schedule.

limitations: The reopening is confirmed by one public source family; independent corroboration is not yet available.

sources.title: Clinic oxygen inspection cleared
sources.excerpt: The oxygen-system inspection passed. The clinic plans to publish its staffing roster before reopening on September 3.

presentation.title: Weekend ferry reliability
presentation.context: When is the new weekend crossing dependable enough to plan around?

whatChanged.text: The board authorized an October 4 start, but the operator has not assigned crews, so that date remains a target rather than a dependable launch.

whyItMatters.text: Do not book a fixed connection around the new timetable yet; political approval has not become an operating commitment.

watchNext.text: Treat a published crew roster or October 4 ticket inventory as the confirmation that resolves the conflict.

limitations: The governing decision and the operator bulletin disagree about launch readiness.

sources.title: Weekend crews remain unassigned
sources.excerpt: No crews are assigned to the weekend crossing. The operator will confirm a launch only after rosters and ticket inventory are published.

presentation.title: Electric delivery fleet
presentation.context: How should the fleet meet the new zone deadline without sacrificing delivery reliability?

whatChanged.text: The zero-emission zone now has a fixed January 1 start, while winter field data shows a 28% range penalty that the route plan does not yet absorb.

whyItMatters.text: A fleet-wide purchase before a cold-weather route test could trade compliance risk for missed deliveries.

testNow.text: ChatGPT judgment: Run 12 matched routes over 14 days, pairing one electric van with one current van on distance and payload; compare completion rate and charging delay.

deferUntil.text: ChatGPT judgment: Defer the fleet-wide purchase until all 12 routes finish with at least 20% reserve and the depot completes one charger-outage drill.

rollbackIf.text: ChatGPT judgment: Roll back if more than 1 of 12 routes misses its delivery window or median turnaround is over 15% slower during the 14-day run.

limitations: The field report covers comparable vans, not this fleet's routes or depot.

sources.title: Zero-emission zone begins January 1
sources.excerpt: The authority confirmed that the commercial zero-emission zone begins January 1.

sources.title: Cold-weather electric van field report
sources.excerpt: Matched field routes recorded a 28% median winter range penalty and longer turnaround when charging queues formed.

sources.title: Charger resilience drill guidance
sources.excerpt: Operators should validate an outage drill before depending on one depot for route-critical charging.

normalizedDecisionText: Run 12 matched routes over 14 days, pairing one electric van with one current van on distance and payload; compare completion rate and charging delay.
Defer the fleet-wide purchase until all 12 routes finish with at least 20% reserve and the depot completes one charger-outage drill.
Roll back if more than 1 of 12 routes misses its delivery window or median turnaround is over 15% slower during the 14-day run.

required.startsWith: Summer watering drops to two mornings a week
The garden can keep its harvest target
Recheck the plan if reservoir storage falls below 45%

presentation.title: Drought-resilient community garden
presentation.context: How can the garden protect its summer harvest under tighter watering limits?

whatChanged.text: Summer watering drops to two mornings a week on June 1, while the new planting guide shifts beans and greens toward shorter-cycle varieties.

whyItMatters.text: The garden can keep its harvest target by moving water-hungry beds to drip lines and favoring crops that mature inside the tighter watering window.

watchNext.text: Recheck the plan if reservoir storage falls below 45%, the published trigger for the next restriction stage.

sources.title: Stage Two summer watering limits
sources.excerpt: From June 1, community gardens may water on two mornings each week. Stage Three begins if reservoir storage falls below 45%.

sources.title: Short-cycle crops for restricted watering
sources.excerpt: The revised guide recommends drip irrigation and shorter-cycle bean and green varieties under two-day watering schedules.
